patch_description: The current program relies purely on random restarts, wasting much of its 7s budget rediscovering good basins. For the Heilbronn n=11 problem, the best configurations place most points on the boundary (vertices and edge subdivisions) with a few interior points — small triangles always have boundary points. Two improvements: (1) seed restarts with structured warm starts (vertices + edge lattices + triangular grid, slightly jittered to avoid degenerate zero-area collinear starts that trap local search), in addition to random starts; (2) wrap restarts in a time budget (up to ~20s) so more restarts run, using best-of-N. Also try the three edge-move variants (slide along boundary) in the perturbation batch since boundary points are what the optimum uses — adding a few tangent-slide candidates to the K Gaussian candidates increases the chance of improving moves when the worst point lies on an edge.
